english: the product of the nine factors $\log_{1+kx}\left(1+(k+1)x\right)$, $k=1,2,\ldots,9$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0^{+}}\dfrac{10-P(x)}{x}$ is ______.
hindi: जो $k=1,2,\ldots,9$ के लिए नौ गुणनखंडों $\log_{1+kx}\left(1+(k+1)x\right)$ का गुणनफल है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0^{+}}\dfrac{10-P(x)}{x}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Change of base: $\log_{1+kx}(1+(k+1)x)=\dfrac{\ln(1+(k+1)x)}{\ln(1+kx)}$, so the product telescopes:
solution_full: Each factor is defined for $x\in\left(0,\dfrac1{10}\right)$: every base $1+kx>1$ and every argument is positive.
In the product over $k=1,\ldots,9$ the numerator of each factor cancels the denominator of the next, leaving $P(x)=\dfrac{\ln(1+10x)}{\ln(1+x)}$.
So $P(x)\to10$ as $x\to0^{+}$ and the limit is of the form $\dfrac00$.
(In general the product up to base $1+(n-1)x$ gives $\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$; here $n=10$.)
originality_note: New: a telescoping chain of variable-base logarithms whose bases and arguments are 1 + kx collapses to ln(1+10x)/ln(1+x), and the second-order term of this ratio is asked (way 5). Closest known: the constant product log_2 3 . log_3 4 ... log_{n} (n+1) = log_2 (n+1), and lim ln(1+ax)/ln(1+bx) = a/b. Different because: the telescoped value tends to 10, so the question needs the next term of the log expansions, not the first-order ratio.

concept_use.Logarithmic identities: product, quotien: Change of base makes the nine-factor product telescope to ln(1+10x)/ln(1+x).
concept_use.Evaluation of limit involving exponentia: The limit is found from the expansion ln(1+u) = u - u^2/2 + ... of both logarithms to second order.
